title: How Do AI Search Engines Recommend Products?
excerpt: How ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini choose which products to recommend, based on official documentation, and how to improve your visibility.
author: AI Brand Track Team
content:
## Quick Answer

AI search engines recommend products by interpreting what the user wants, then combining what the model learned in training with information retrieved from the web, such as product data, reviews and comparison articles. OpenAI, for example, [says ChatGPT's product results consider](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-shopping-with-chatgpt-search) the user's query and context, structured product metadata from first- and third-party providers, and the answer the model generates before it looks at new search results. Your brand's presence in those sources largely determines whether ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google Gemini recommend your products.

## Introduction

An AI assistant may have just recommended your competitor's product instead of yours, and the buyer may never have questioned it.

Product discovery can now happen in AI conversations, not just on search result pages. When someone asks Claude "what's the best project management tool" or ChatGPT "recommend a CRM for a small business," the products named in the answer make the shortlist. Products the assistant doesn't mention are easy to miss.

This is where answer engine optimization comes in. Our guide to [answer engine optimization](/answer-engine-optimization) covers the broader discipline; this article focuses on how product recommendations actually get made.

## What Are AI Search Engines and How Do They Recommend Products?

AI search engines are conversational assistants that understand natural-language questions and answer in prose, often naming specific products. Unlike a traditional results page, they put recommendations directly in the answer.

Assistants like these draw on two kinds of information: what their underlying model learned during training, and, when they search, what they retrieve from the web at the time of the question. Combining a model with retrieved documents is known as retrieval-augmented generation, described in the [original RAG paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401).

The process looks like this: a user asks a question, the assistant interprets the intent, optionally searches for current information, and generates an answer that may name specific products.

Your brand either appears in that answer or the buyer moves on without it.

## How Do AI Search Engines Decide Which Products to Recommend?

We're not aware of most AI providers publishing detailed ranking rules. OpenAI is an exception: its help article on [shopping with ChatGPT search](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-shopping-with-chatgpt-search) explains how product results are selected. Combined with what's known about how LLMs work, that gives a useful picture.

### What Role Does Training Data Play in Product Recommendations?

Training data is the foundation of what a model "knows." [OpenAI says](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed) its models are trained on publicly available internet data, data accessed through partnerships, and data provided by users, trainers and researchers, all collected before a cutoff date.

In our experience, brands discussed often and in relevant contexts (industry publications, review sites, community forums, expert articles) are more likely to be associated with their category in the model's knowledge. A brand that appears in many independent comparisons is generally better represented than one that appears in a few.

This also means new brands, or brands with little third-party coverage, start at a disadvantage when the model answers from memory.

### How Does Web Retrieval Influence AI Product Suggestions?

All four major assistants can search the web: [ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), [Claude](https://claude.com/resources/articles/web-search), [Perplexity](https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352895-how-does-perplexity-work) and Gemini (which can [ground answers in Google Search](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search)). When they do, they read current pages and usually cite them.

That means fresh, well-ranked content matters. A comparison article or review roundup that ranks for your category today can shape today's answers.

[OpenAI says](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-shopping-with-chatgpt-search) that when determining which products to surface, ChatGPT considers structured metadata from first-party and third-party providers (such as price and product description) and other third-party content. Accurate, consistent product data across your site and listings therefore matters.

### What Is Conversation Context and Why Does It Matter?

Assistants interpret each question in the context of the conversation. Context shapes recommendations significantly.

Someone asking for "affordable email marketing tools" gets different suggestions from someone asking for "enterprise email platforms with advanced automation." [OpenAI's example](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-shopping-with-chatgpt-search): if you specify a $30 budget, ChatGPT focuses more on price.

Follow-up messages refine the answer. If a user says "that's too expensive" or "I need better analytics," the assistant adjusts. ChatGPT can also consider saved context such as [Memory and custom instructions](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-shopping-with-chatgpt-search).

Your brand needs visibility across the different use cases and buyer profiles you serve, not just one generic "best" question.

### Does Popularity Affect Which Products AI Recommends?

Indirectly. We haven't seen any provider say they rank products by how many users asked about them, so be skeptical of claims that assistants use collaborative filtering like a store's "customers also bought."

What does happen is that popular products tend to have more reviews, more comparison articles and more discussion online. That gives the model more to learn from and more pages to retrieve. In our experience, well-known products are mentioned more, and lesser-known ones need deliberate effort to build their footprint.

### What Role Do Brand Mentions and Citations Play?

Mentions across the web create associations between your brand and specific use cases. When reviewers, comparison articles and experts consistently describe your product as a fit for a particular need, in our experience assistants are more likely to recommend it for that need.

Specific, substantive coverage helps more than passing references. A detailed review explaining who a product is best for gives an assistant much more to work with than a one-line mention.

Specificity matters in your own content too. "Built for e-commerce teams that need abandoned-cart automation" tells an AI exactly when to recommend you; "a great email tool" doesn't.

### How Do Reviews and Sentiment Affect Product Recommendations?

Assistants synthesize what sources say about a product. [OpenAI says](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-shopping-with-chatgpt-search) ChatGPT may consider reviews when choosing products, and that the review summaries it shows are model-generated from reviews on public websites, which OpenAI does not verify.

Consistently positive coverage makes a product easier to recommend. In our experience, mixed coverage often leads to caveats like "some users report issues with customer support."

Managing your reputation across review sites and communities therefore affects how AI describes you.

## Why Does AI Product Recommendation Matter for Your Brand?

In our view, AI-assisted discovery is a meaningful shift in how people research purchases.

### How Has Consumer Research Behavior Changed with AI?

Traditional search meant clicking several links, reading reviews and comparing tabs. An AI assistant can summarize options in one answer.

Research on Google's AI summaries shows the effect on clicks: [Pew Research Center](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/) found that in March 2025, users who saw an AI summary clicked a traditional search result in 8% of visits, compared with 15% for those who didn't. When the answer is on the page, fewer people click through to compare.

### What Happens When AI Never Recommends Your Product?

If ChatGPT never mentions your CRM, buyers who rely on it may never consider it.

Competitors mentioned consistently get into more shortlists by default, and buyers may assume AI recommendations reflect the best available options.

Traditional SEO still drives traffic, but AI answers can also shape which brands get considered.

### How Do AI Recommendations Affect Brand Perception?

A buyer may treat an AI recommendation as a kind of neutral third-party opinion. Being recommended can add credibility, especially for newer brands.

Established brands that aren't mentioned risk the opposite: buyers may wonder why the assistant didn't include them.

## How Can You Increase Your Product's Visibility in AI Search Engines?

Building AI visibility combines content, third-party coverage, technical basics and regular measurement.

### Step 1: How Do You Audit Current AI Visibility?

Start by testing how AI assistants currently treat your brand. Ask ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google Gemini the questions your customers ask.

Vary the questions: "best [product category]," "recommend a [solution] for [use case]," and "[your brand] vs [competitor]."

Record every response: whether your brand appears, in what context, with what sentiment, and which competitors appear alongside it. Use fresh conversations, and repeat key questions, since [answers vary between runs](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed).

Manual testing is slow and inconsistent, which is where dedicated tools help.

### Step 2: What Content Improves AI Recommendations?

Create clear, well-structured content that answers buyer questions directly.

Publish guides like "How to Choose [Product Category] for [Specific Use Case]," including honest comparisons with alternatives.

Publish real customer stories with outcomes you have permission to share. Concrete details help both buyers and AI understand who your product suits.

Use clear headings, direct answers near the top of each section, and specific facts such as pricing, features and integrations. Google's guidance on [helpful, reliable, people-first content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) is a good standard.

Keep existing content current: update pricing, features and examples when they change.

### Step 3: How Do You Build Coverage Across Trusted Sources?

Earn mentions in publications and sites that cover your category. Offer expert commentary, and get included in relevant comparison roundups.

Pitch genuine customer stories and original data to relevant media.

Participate authentically in Reddit, Quora and industry forums. Helpful contributions, not promotion, are what get discussed and referenced.

Invite satisfied customers to leave detailed reviews on the review sites that matter in your category. Specific reviews help AI understand your strengths.

### Step 4: Does Structured Data Help AI Understanding?

Structured data helps search engines understand your pages, and it's good practice for product sites. Implement [Product structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product) on product pages, including name, description, brand, offers and, where eligible, ratings and reviews. Add Organization markup with your logo and official profiles.

Keep expectations realistic. Google states that there are [no additional requirements or special optimizations](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) needed to appear in its AI features, and it [reduced FAQ and HowTo rich results in 2023](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/08/howto-faq-changes). Treat schema as part of solid technical SEO, not as a dedicated lever for AI recommendations.

Validate your markup, since errors make it less useful.

### Step 5: How Do You Monitor and Measure AI Recommendation Performance?

Test the same questions on a regular schedule. Track where your brand appears in AI answers and note new competitors entering the shortlist.

Measure share of voice: how often your brand appears compared with competitors. See our guide to [AI share of voice](/blog/ai-share-of-voice).

Watch sentiment so you can catch negative patterns early.

Compare AI visibility trends with referral traffic from AI platforms and conversion data.

## Frequently Asked Questions About How AI Search Engines Recommend Products

### Do AI search engines favor certain brands or industries?

We haven't seen evidence of intentional favoritism, but in our experience well-documented products with lots of independent coverage appear more often, and established brands with years of reviews and articles have an advantage. Newer brands can close the gap by building specific, credible coverage for the use cases they serve.

### Can you pay to appear in AI product recommendations?

Not in the organic answers, according to the providers that have addressed it. OpenAI began testing ads in ChatGPT in the US on February 9, 2026, for users on the Free and Go plans. Its [ads help article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001047-ads-in-chatgpt) says ads appear below responses, are clearly labeled, and don't influence ChatGPT's answers, and its [shopping help article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-shopping-with-chatgpt-search) says product results are not ads. Paid placement and organic recommendations are separate.

### How often do AI recommendations change?

Answers can change when providers release new models, when web search results change, and simply between runs because [generation involves sampling](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed). That makes regular measurement more useful than a one-time check.

### What's the difference between AI recommendations and traditional search results?

Traditional search shows ranked links that users evaluate themselves. AI assistants suggest specific products in the answer, usually with reasons. That's convenient for buyers, but it narrows the set of options they see.

### How long does it take to improve AI visibility for your product?

It varies. Answers based on live web search can change once new or updated pages start being retrieved. Answers drawn from a model's training data may not change until a future model version. Measure regularly to see what's moving.

### Can negative reviews prevent AI from recommending your product?

They influence how assistants describe a product but don't automatically exclude it. In our experience, assistants often mention products with caveats about known issues, and consistently negative coverage makes recommendations less likely, so addressing the underlying issues and responding to reviews helps.

### Do all AI platforms recommend products the same way?

No. Each uses different models, training data and search systems, so the same question can produce different shortlists on ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini. Track all of them rather than assuming one represents the rest.

### How important are product reviews for AI recommendations?

Important. Reviews are a major source of information about strengths, weaknesses and ideal customers, and [OpenAI lists reviews](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-shopping-with-chatgpt-search) among the factors ChatGPT may consider for product results. Detailed, specific reviews are more useful than short generic ones.

## Conclusion: Win the AI Recommendation Game

AI search engines recommend products based on what their models learned and what they find when they search: product data, reviews, comparisons and discussion. Brands with accurate, specific and widely covered information are the easiest to recommend.

The good news is that this is something you can work on. Improve your own content, earn credible third-party coverage, keep product data accurate, and measure the results.

You can't improve what you don't measure, and traditional analytics won't tell you whether ChatGPT recommends you or your competitor.
